tasks.desc: Ideation: select coordinate-compressed Fenwick + O(kn) prefix DP as primary; two-heaps as fallback.

Implement the full solution using coordinate-compressed Fenwick trees: compute cost[start] for every length-x window by maintaining count/sum trees and lower-median rank (x+1)//2, then run two-row prefix DP dp[t][i] = min(dp[t][i-1], dp[t-1][i-x] + cost[i-x]) to return dp[k][n]; include tests on the provided examples and small random brute force.
Verify correctness on edge cases: x = n, k = 1, adjacent non-overlapping windows, duplicate values, negative values, and large costs.
If the Fenwick implementation fails or is too slow, switch to a two-heaps sliding-median implementation with lazy deletion and reuse the same DP.

proposals: Try the coordinate-compressed Fenwick tree approach first: maintain count and sum trees for the sliding window, compute every window median cost, then run a two-row O(kn) prefix DP for choosing k non-overlapping windows.
Try the two-heaps sliding-median approach as a second implementation: maintain lower/upper heaps with logical sizes, sums, and lazy deletion, then use the same interval DP.
Try a static wavelet matrix or persistent segment tree for range median and range sum as a fallback if sliding maintenance becomes too bug-prone.
Try the start-position DP with running prefix minima as an alternative to the prefix-length DP to verify the non-overlap off-by-one behavior.
Keep min-cost flow or k-layer DAG shortest path only as a correctness-check reduction, not as the main solution, because it is likely overkill for the given constraints.
